context.passage:
Lewis Contemporary Art Museum (LCAM) Lecture Series

LCAM is hosting a lecture series in June to celebrate its tenth anniversary.
A dmission is free for LCAM members and $10 per lecture for the general public.
Space is limited, so register early. Walk-ins are allowed if space permits. All lectures
begin at 8:00 P.M. and are held in the LCAM auditorium.

June 3-Looking at Plebani

Dr. Juan Rodriguez, a professor at Northern University, will explore the textile works
of Smithtown's most prolific artist, Marcia Plebani. He will discuss Plebani's most
important works, including her Watching Birds series.

June 10-Jerry Wadley's Turning Points

LCAM artistic director Hyejeong Kim will examine how Jerry Wadley's style evolved
over his 70-year career. Dr. Kim will focus on how Mr. Wadley's sculptures came to
capture the beauty and mystery of ordinary people.

June 17-Our Views
Dr. A yano Goto, a professor at Rampel University, will discuss a selection of
landscape paintings by Ara Na, focusing on why and how Na chooses which
landscapes to paint.

June 24-The Photographs of Lily Losaru

LCAM associate curator Emilio Loria will delve into Lily Losaru's photography. He
will show how Ms. Losaru uses portrait photography to reflect the interests and
personalities of her subjects.

To: | | rplatt@Icam.org |
Ce: | | eloria@Icam.org |
From: | | agoto@rampel.edu |
Date: | | May 20 |
Subject: {| Lecture at LCAM |

Dear Mr. Platt,

Good morning. I have just been asked to give the keynote address at a conference next
month. Unfortunately, the date of the conference conflicts with the scheduled date of my
lecture at LCAM. I apologize for the inconvenience.

I have taken the liberty of communicating with Dr. Emilio Loria, whom I have known for
many years, and he has graciously agreed to swap lecture dates with me if needed.
A lternatively, I could give my lecture in July. Let me know whether either option is
viable.

Sincerely,

A yano Goto
Professor, Rampel University

To: | | agoto@rampel.edu

Ce: | | eloria@Icam.org
From: | | rplatt@Icam.org
Date: | | May 21

Subject: | | RE: Lecture at LCAM

Dear Dr. Goto,

Thank you for letting us know about your scheduling conflict. We believe the swapping
option is better. We avoid hosting events in July-our museum tends to be low on staff
throughout the month.

By the way, we are currently designing the lecture series program and would like to
include an image of one of the artworks you will discuss. Do you have a preference?

Sincerely,

Ron Platt, LCAM Programming
